scope: Manual seven-class reading of the exact current physical enclosure articles. Current cleanup parts were read after their matching publication was live; unchanged articles retain their exact physical-byte readings. Named mating profiles, working flexures and user-selected sections have individual reasons and alternatives. Unintended cavity and mount cut remnants are removed. This is a manual review, not an automatic gate or physical strength/support-removal qualification.

answer_entries.reason: Specific fitted M3 insert-host interface: these condenser-finger samples span 2.000 mm from the purchased insert pilot to the outer finger boundary. The Ruthex RX-series table specifies a 4.0 mm pilot and 1.6 mm minimum surrounding wall for RX-M3x5.7. This retained local section meets that dimensional guidance; native correspondence identifies the pre-dock interface. It does not qualify installed pullout or finger load capacity.
answer_entries.alternatives: A larger host changes the donor-flange and driver-approach envelope. Keep the manufacturer-compatible pilot and host while qualifying actual insert retention and loaded finger performance.

answer_entries.reason: Unavoidable lifting interfaces: these Z29.25 handhold ceilings retain the flat finger bearings, shared R6 ends and 12 mm roof sections. Support can leave through the open handhold and seam before assembly. Actual cleanup, bare-surface comfort and loaded lifting remain unqualified.
answer_entries.alternatives: Sloping changes the finger bearing and opening. Filling below the roof blocks upward entry. Retain the specified working profile and assess its support contacts in the production slice.

answer_entries.reason: Unavoidable square capture interfaces: these Z169.2 flats are the front rail catches. Their opposing feet retain the native 0.50 mm running/support allowance. The flat overlap resists lifting after that play is taken up. Support can leave the open rail lane before assembly; removal effort remains unqualified.
answer_entries.alternatives: Sloping introduces a camming bearing. Filling the lane enters foot travel; removing the overlap loses capture.

answer_entries.reason: The linter is wrong for this channel: this 45° face is the roof of the relief over the lower Y-stack screw passage where it crosses front-bottom's knuckle underside (`_y_bore_reliefs`). It rises toward the passage inside a slot of the passage's own width, so both of its rising edges stand on the slot's walls 5.2 mm apart and each layer of it is carried at both ends as well as by the layer below; the rule reads one wall and its rising edge, a slope hanging sideways off a single wall.
answer_entries.alternatives: A level roof over the slot is a down-facing ceiling. A roof rising off the slot walls, a gable, dives under the 45° knuckle face along a V and leaves a ridge down the slot. A vertical end wall where the roof lands meets the knuckle face on a 45° arris. The rule could count a slope whose two rising edges stand on opposed walls as carried.

answer_entries.reason: Approved by Derek as drawn: each reading is a vent bar of the condenser vents on front-bottom's two flanks, the mullion between two slots struck down the floors of neighbouring flute grooves (enclosure README, The condenser's vents). Each reads 1.834 mm, the mullion between its two slots at the groove floor. Derek, 2026-10-21: "I am good with and I approve the vent bars."
answer_entries.alternatives: Wider mullions narrow the 3.1 mm slots and the open area the condenser's fan draws through; fewer slots close it further.

answer_entries.reason: Functional retaining underside of the approved J11 gas-sensor cable hook. The 0.75 mm projection closes the 2.20 mm seat to a 1.45 mm entry mouth for nominal 1.70 mm insulation, matching the accepted 4P cable clip's entry section. Its flat underside catches the conductors after insertion. The projection and mouth supply the required retention geometry; the hook's structural section is 3 mm.
answer_entries.alternatives: A 3 mm projection closes this seat completely; keeping the mouth with that projection requires a 4.45 mm deep seat, adding 2.25 mm of cable movement behind the catch. Reducing the projection opens the mouth toward the cable diameter. Sloping the underside supplies an exit ramp in place of the flat catch.

answer_entries.reason: Functional flat catch of the approved J11 gas-sensor cable hook, using the accepted 4P clip's 0.75 mm retaining projection and 1.45 mm mouth for nominal 1.70 mm insulation. Its underside retains the four leads after insertion; the 45 degree entry is on the opposite side.
answer_entries.alternatives: A sloped underside lets the cable cam back through the mouth. Increasing the projection to 3 mm requires a 4.45 mm deep seat to preserve the mouth, adding 2.25 mm of movement behind the catch. Filling the entry prevents insertion from above.
